metadata.title: NZ 2026 Policy Tracker
metadata.note: Only explicit, decided 2026 election commitments from official party sources are shown.

policies.title: Economy and cost of living delivery record
policies.summary: National says its current work is focused on rebuilding the economy, easing cost pressures, cutting red tape, supporting trade and investment, and creating conditions for higher incomes.

policies.title: Fiscal plan and tax relief
policies.summary: National's older fiscal plan set out a disciplined-spending, lower-tax, lower-debt approach while maintaining funding for frontline services and infrastructure.

policies.title: Quality, timely healthcare
policies.summary: National says it is delivering more doctors, nurses, medicines, health targets, local urgent care, and easier access to healthcare as part of its current government programme.

policies.title: Teaching the Basics Brilliantly
policies.summary: National says it has mandated daily reading, writing and maths, banned cell-phone use in schools, introduced structured teaching, proposed replacing NCEA, and expanded learning support.

policies.title: Restoring law and order
policies.summary: National says it has reduced violent crime and ram raids, increased police patrols, restricted gang patches, restored Three Strikes, capped sentence discounts, and agreed a methamphetamine harm plan.

policies.title: Blueprint for a Better Environment
policies.summary: National's older environment policy covered freshwater, biodiversity, climate, oceans, waste and planning-law reform, with an emphasis on environmental outcomes alongside growth.

policies.title: Public service overhaul and workforce target
policies.summary: National says the Government will overhaul the core public service by reducing the number of departments, expanding digital and AI tools, restoring core public service staffing to about 55,000 by mid-2029, and targeting $2.4 billion in savings over four years.

policies.title: Three free doctor's visits with Medicard
policies.summary: Labour says every New Zealander would receive three free doctor's visits each year through a new Medicard, funded by targeted property tax changes.

policies.title: Targeted capital gains tax
policies.summary: Labour proposes a 28% tax on profit made after 1 July 2027 when commercial or residential investment property is sold, excluding the family home, farms, KiwiSaver, shares, businesses, inheritances and personal items.

policies.title: New Zealand Future Fund
policies.summary: Labour says the New Zealand Future Fund would invest in infrastructure and innovative New Zealand businesses to support secure jobs and keep more ideas, wealth and people in New Zealand.

policies.title: Free cervical screening
policies.summary: Labour says cervical screening would be free for people aged 25 to 69, loaded onto the Medicard, and funded from baseline health funding from the 2027/28 financial year.

policies.title: Family Doctor Loan Scheme
policies.summary: Labour proposes up to 50 loans each year to help doctors buy into or establish owner-operated general practices, prioritising areas with no GPs or closed books, with 10-year repayment and interest-free first two years.

policies.title: Flatter tax and less regulation
policies.summary: ACT says it wants careful government spending, lower taxes, less red tape, a two-rate income tax system with a 28% top rate, and fewer barriers to investment, jobs and wage growth.

policies.title: Health accountability and public-private delivery
policies.summary: ACT says health services should be timely and based on individual need, with public-private partnerships, measurable Health NZ targets, transparency, and less bureaucracy.

policies.title: Restoring law and order
policies.summary: ACT says government should protect safety and property, restore consequences for offenders, focus police on frontline crime-fighting, and use rehabilitation incentives for prisoners who gain skills.

policies.title: Education choice and accountability
policies.summary: ACT supports parent choice across public, private and partnership schools, core knowledge in reading, writing, maths, science and history, stronger NCEA accountability, and a Student Education Account system.

policies.title: Infrastructure planning and delivery
policies.summary: ACT says infrastructure should be delivered efficiently with long-term planning, lower red tape, private investment where appropriate, user-pays approaches, property-rights protections, and decentralised decision-making.

policies.title: Policy page and coalition agreement
policies.summary: New Zealand First's policy page currently points readers to its 2023 election policies and to the coalition agreement commitments it says are supported by National and ACT in government.

policies.title: Economic coalition achievements
policies.summary: New Zealand First lists achieved coalition commitments including a banking competition inquiry, assessing inflation's effect on average tax rates by or before 2026, and increased funding for IRD tax audits.

policies.title: Law and order 2023 policy
policies.summary: NZ First's 2023 policy proposed at least 500 new frontline police in the first 18 months, more Youth Aid officers, mandatory sentences for assaults on first responders, and stronger sentencing policies.

policies.title: Health and PHARMAC 2023 policy
policies.summary: NZ First's 2023 health policy proposed revisiting GP funding, increasing primary-care funding, mobile health buses, more diagnostic access, and a larger PHARMAC budget with rapid access funding for innovative medicines.

policies.title: Education and skills 2023 policy
policies.summary: NZ First's 2023 policy emphasised core skills, learning support, links between education and employment, STEM incentives, third-year fees-free tertiary study, and free apprenticeships for in-demand vocations.

policies.title: Agriculture and emissions 2023 policy
policies.summary: NZ First's 2023 agriculture policy opposed agriculture emissions pricing unless adopted by trading partners, supported farm-level reporting, and proposed incentives for emissions-reduction technologies.

policies.title: Green Budget 2025
policies.summary: The Green Budget 2025 sets out an alternative budget with free GPs and dental, free early childhood education, nature restoration, clean energy, whenua return, and a fairer tax system to fund it.

policies.title: Fiscal Strategy
policies.summary: The Green fiscal strategy argues for fiscal management focused on wellbeing, climate resilience, public investment, economic sovereignty, and recognising the costs of underinvestment.

policies.title: Health Policy
policies.summary: The Green health policy calls for preventive care, reducing disparities, fully funded public provision of dental care, GP clinics, ambulance, emergency, aged, palliative and mental-health services, plus fair conditions for health workers.

policies.title: Education Policy
policies.summary: The Green education policy supports inclusive, accessible and democratic education, free quality education, Te Tiriti-centred learning, fully funded free ECE, fees-free tertiary education, and writing off student loan debt.

policies.title: Climate Change Policy
policies.summary: The Green climate policy calls for Te Tiriti-based climate solutions, energy sufficiency and democratisation, sustainable transport, phasing out fossil fuels, agricultural diversification, adaptation planning, and just transitions.

policies.title: Livelihoods Policy
policies.summary: The Green livelihoods policy supports liveable income support, accessible welfare services, a legal right to a minimum income, protections against exploitative lending, and basic services that support wellbeing.

policies.title: 2026 policy platform status
policies.summary: Te Pāti Māori's main policy page currently says the party is working on its policies and will be back soon, so current 2026 policy entries should be reviewed when the platform is published.

policies.title: Mana Motuhake
policies.summary: The Mana Motuhake policy calls for constitutional transformation, a Māori Parliament, implementing Matike Mai recommendations, recognising Aotearoa as the official name, land return measures, binding Waitangi Tribunal recommendations, and stronger Te Tiriti oversight.

policies.title: Education and training
policies.summary: Te Pāti Māori's education policy centres on resourcing kaupapa Māori education, overhauling the mainstream system, directing more budget to Māori models of delivery, free digital access, and pathways through STEM, trades and apprenticeships.

policies.title: Prisons position statement
policies.summary: A January 2026 Te Pāti Māori statement says the party stands behind its policy of creating an Aotearoa where prisons are not needed, arguing prisons do not address root causes such as poverty, inequality, unemployment, homelessness, racism, poor mental health and trauma.

policies.title: Call to publish gender-affirming care guidelines
policies.summary: Te Pāti Māori has called for Te Whatu Ora to publish updated gender-affirming healthcare guidelines, saying clinical guidance should be led by experts and that withholding the guidelines causes harm to trans and non-binary people.

officialSource.label: Te Pāti Māori gender-affirming care statement

policies.title: 2026 State of the Nation response
policies.summary: Te Pāti Māori's January 2026 response to the Prime Minister's State of the Nation speech argues the Government is building a post-Treaty state and criticises the absence of Te Tiriti, tangata whenua, rangatiratanga, iwi, hapū, whānau, kaitiakitanga and mana motuhake from the speech.

officialSource.label: Te Pāti Māori State of the Nation response

policies.title: Tax Reset
policies.summary: Opportunity proposes a Citizen's Income of up to $370 a week for most adults, funded through a 1.75% annual land value tax, alongside compulsory KiwiSaver contributions that would rise over time to 6% for employees and employers.

policies.title: Healthy People
policies.summary: Opportunity proposes ten-year cross-party health planning, more primary and preventive care, proper funding for core services and infrastructure, improved workforce pay and training, and reinstatement of smokefree legislation.

policies.title: Future-fit Education
policies.summary: Opportunity proposes stronger community and parent-led early childhood education, smaller centres and improved ratios, ECE teacher pay parity, civics from Year 6, wider learning support, teacher development and more flexible lifelong learning.

policies.title: Abundant Energy
policies.summary: Opportunity proposes a cross-party target to add 30GW of renewable generation by 2050, a capacity investment scheme, consolidated energy regulation and distribution, and low-interest finance for household and community electrification.

policies.title: Healthy Oceans
policies.summary: Opportunity proposes ecosystem-based fisheries management, a phase-out of bottom trawling, cameras on commercial fishing boats, protection of 30% of ocean territory by 2035, opposition to seabed mining and investment in a sustainable blue economy.

policies.title: Smart on Crime
policies.summary: Opportunity proposes more funding for courts and probation, decriminalising drug possession while retaining penalties for supply, expanding rehabilitation and specialist courts, and raising the youth court jurisdiction age.

policies.title: Intergenerational Infrastructure
policies.summary: Opportunity proposes an expert-led 30-year infrastructure framework, higher public and local-government investment, free public transport, faster project approvals, appropriate user-pays and value-capture funding, and mandatory asset-management standards.

policies.title: Honouring Te Tiriti
policies.summary: Opportunity proposes repealing the Treaty Principles Bill and the Marine and Coastal Area amendment bill if passed, teaching Aotearoa history and Te Tiriti throughout education, supporting te reo teachers, devolving selected services with resources and autonomy, and equitable Treaty settlements.

policies.title: Lift KiwiSaver contributions to 12%
policies.summary: National says an elected National Government would raise default employee and employer KiwiSaver contributions by 0.5 percentage points a year from April 2029, reaching 6% each and 12% combined in 2032.

policies.title: Restrict commercial fishing in the Hauraki Gulf
policies.summary: National says it will reinstate the ban on all fishing in the Hauraki Gulf's High Protection Areas and review the decision allowing bottom trawling in designated Gulf corridors if re-elected.

policies.title: Extend paid parental leave to 30 weeks
policies.summary: National says a re-elected government would gradually extend paid parental leave from 26 to 30 weeks by 2029, let parents overlap or divide the entitlement, and protect full holiday pay after returning to work.

policies.title: Weekly public transport fare cap
policies.summary: Labour proposes a weekly public transport fare cap from July 2027 of $20 in Auckland, Wellington and Christchurch and $10 elsewhere, covering buses, trains and selected ferries.

policies.title: Free prescriptions
policies.summary: Labour proposes removing the $5 prescription charge from July 2027 for everyone entitled to publicly funded healthcare, funded through its targeted capital gains tax.

policies.title: Free maternity scans
policies.summary: Labour proposes making all referred maternity scans free nationwide from July 2028 and funding 24 paid trainee sonographer positions.

policies.title: Expand Apprenticeship Boost
policies.summary: Labour proposes extending employer payments to two years, giving new apprentices a $1,000 toolbox grant, adding five trade areas and piloting structured mentoring.

policies.title: SolarSaver
policies.summary: Labour proposes subsidies and low-cost finance to help homeowners, renters and communities install or access solar energy without the upfront cost.

policies.title: A tax system for all of us
policies.summary: The Greens propose a 2.5% tax on net assets above $10 million excluding family homes, tax on gifts or inheritances above $1 million with exemptions, higher taxes on large corporations and a $10,000 income-tax-free threshold.

policies.title: Drink, Swim, Fish
policies.summary: The Greens' current freshwater policy announcement proposes changing water rules to restore safe drinking water and clean waterways for swimming and fishing.

policies.title: Power for all of us
policies.summary: The Greens' current energy policy focuses on lower power bills, cleaner renewable generation and greater public ownership of the electricity system.

policies.title: Tax
policies.summary: Te Pāti Māori proposes making the wealthiest pay more and using the revenue for housing, health, education and whānau support.

policies.title: Economic development
policies.summary: Te Pāti Māori proposes Māori-led institutions and funds for enterprise, trade and innovation, long-term Māori wealth building, and protection of Māori data and knowledge.

officialSource.label: Te Pāti Māori economic development policy

policies.title: Health
policies.summary: Te Pāti Māori proposes rebuilding and strengthening Māori-led health authority and services, shifting toward prevention and whānau wellbeing, and making care accessible, culturally safe and accountable.

policies.title: Education and Training
policies.summary: Te Pāti Māori proposes a Māori-led education authority, embedding mātauranga Māori across learning, removing barriers to training and strengthening Māori governance in education.

policies.title: Kai Sovereignty
policies.summary: Te Pāti Māori proposes protecting Māori food systems and seed sovereignty, investing in community food systems and regenerative Māori agriculture, supporting Māori-owned supermarkets and increasing access to land for food production.

officialSource.label: Te Pāti Māori Kai Sovereignty policy

policies.title: Justice
policies.summary: Te Pāti Māori proposes Māori-led justice authority and community solutions, reforming laws that criminalise poverty and moving away from mass imprisonment.

policies.title: Mana Motuhake
policies.summary: Te Pāti Māori proposes Te Tiriti-based constitutional change, stronger Māori political authority and governance, and progress on land return and rangatiratanga commitments.

officialSource.label: Te Pāti Māori Mana Motuhake policy

policies.title: Break up the gentailers
policies.summary: New Zealand First proposes separating major electricity generators and retailers, changing wholesale pricing, guaranteeing contracts for new generation and equal buy-back pricing for household-generated power.

policies.title: Break up the supermarket duopoly
policies.summary: New Zealand First proposes splitting Foodstuffs into two nationwide brand-based cooperatives, strengthening competition penalties and enforcement, and introducing faster Commerce Act interventions.

policies.title: Return half of mining royalties to regions
policies.summary: New Zealand First proposes returning 50% of mining royalties to the producing region for local infrastructure and services, alongside clearer mining rules, longer permits, geological surveying and workforce investment.

policies.title: KiwiSaver enrolment from birth
policies.summary: New Zealand First proposes compulsory KiwiSaver enrolment at birth for New Zealand citizens with an immediate $1,000 Crown contribution.

policies.title: Buy back the Bank of New Zealand
policies.summary: New Zealand First proposes buying the Bank of New Zealand back from National Australia Bank to restore New Zealand ownership.

officialSource.label: NZ First New Zealand-owned bank policy

policies.title: Disestablish Auckland's Māori Statutory Board
policies.summary: New Zealand First proposes disestablishing Auckland Council's Independent Māori Statutory Board.

officialSource.label: NZ First Auckland statutory board policy

policies.title: Referendum on Māori seats
policies.summary: New Zealand First proposes holding a referendum on the future of the Māori parliamentary seats.

officialSource.label: NZ First Māori seats referendum policy

policies.title: Marsden Point Special Economic Zone
policies.summary: New Zealand First proposes establishing a Special Economic Zone at Marsden Point.

policies.title: Complete Christ Church Cathedral
policies.summary: New Zealand First proposes an additional $15 million of government funding to progress completion of the Christ Church Cathedral rebuild.

policies.title: Citizens-only voting
policies.summary: New Zealand First proposes changing electoral law so only New Zealand citizens can vote.

policies.title: National subsurface development survey
policies.summary: New Zealand First proposes investing an initial $1 billion over a government term in a national survey and dataset covering energy, geothermal resources and carbon-dioxide storage sites.

policies.title: Breakthrough Economy
policies.summary: Opportunity proposes lifting research and development spending to at least 2% of GDP, expanding technology and accelerator support, strengthening Commerce Commission powers over uncompetitive markets, and supporting small businesses.

policies.title: Citizens' Voice
policies.summary: Opportunity proposes representative, paid Citizens' Assemblies for difficult long-term issues and an independent Parliamentary Commissioner to convene them and report on the Government's response.

policies.title: Clean up Politics
policies.summary: Opportunity proposes tighter political-donation rules, regulation of lobbyists, an independent Anti-Corruption Commission, stronger select committees and Official Information law, and limits on Parliament's use of urgency.

policies.title: Healthy Land
policies.summary: Opportunity proposes more conservation and biosecurity funding, stronger water-quality oversight, support for lower-impact land use, investment in native forestry and biodiversity markets, and a circular plastics economy.

policies.title: Climate Action
policies.summary: Opportunity proposes strengthening the Emissions Trading Scheme, adding agricultural emissions, excluding new exotic forestry, supporting sector adaptation and local flood resilience, and rewarding carbon storage in soil, wetlands and native ecosystems.

policies.title: Affordable Housing
policies.summary: Opportunity proposes using its land value tax to reduce land banking, simplifying zoning and small-home construction, underwriting reputable affordable developments, and supporting low-cost finance and council infrastructure funding for quality builds.

policies.title: Mokopuna Māori
policies.summary: Te Pāti Māori proposes ending the removal pipeline for Māori children, restoring whānau authority, investing in whānau-led care, and making the state accountable for harm caused through uplifts and placements.

officialSource.label: Te Pāti Māori Mokopuna Māori policy

policies.title: Disabilities
policies.summary: Te Pāti Māori proposes supporting Māori-led disability services and decision-making, simplifying access to support, and funding assistance that fits whānau circumstances.

policies.title: Housing
policies.summary: Te Pāti Māori proposes building more public and affordable homes, making it easier to build on Māori and ancestral land, and acting against speculation, land banking and vacant properties.

policies.title: Toi Māori
policies.summary: Te Pāti Māori proposes investing in Toi Māori and Māori creative industries, protecting Māori cultural rights and expressions, and supporting Māori-led arts infrastructure, funding and career pathways.

officialSource.label: Te Pāti Māori Toi Māori policy

policies.title: Te Reo Māori
policies.summary: Te Pāti Māori proposes strengthening and normalising te reo Māori, investing in learning and community-led revitalisation, and making the state accountable for protecting the language.

officialSource.label: Te Pāti Māori te reo policy

policies.title: Sports
policies.summary: Te Pāti Māori proposes investing in sport and community initiatives and supporting rangatahi pathways through local clubs, programmes and facilities.

policies.title: Cost of living
policies.summary: Te Pāti Māori proposes lifting incomes, strengthening welfare support and providing practical cost-of-living relief, including more affordable transport.

policies.title: Takatāpui
policies.summary: Te Pāti Māori proposes protecting the wellbeing, safety and dignity of takatāpui Māori and making public services inclusive, accessible and accountable.

policies.title: Military neutrality
policies.summary: Te Pāti Māori proposes declaring Aotearoa militarily neutral, reviewing military alignments, resetting foreign policy around Pacific and Indigenous relationships, and refocusing Defence on protection, disaster response and Pacific support.

policies.title: Freshwater
policies.summary: Te Pāti Māori proposes asserting Māori rights and authority over freshwater, requiring Māori consent in decisions, protecting water resources and sharing benefits fairly.

policies.title: Climate
policies.summary: Te Pāti Māori proposes banning seabed mining, protecting whenua and moana from extractive industries, investing in resilience for at-risk communities, and supporting regenerative approaches aligned with Māori values.

policies.title: Default union membership for new employees
policies.summary: The Greens propose making union membership the default for new employees, with workers able to opt out, and say the policy will be taken into the 2026 election.

policies.title: Withdraw from the Paris Agreement
policies.summary: New Zealand First says it will campaign in the 2026 election for New Zealand to withdraw from the Paris Agreement.

officialSource.label: NZ First Paris Agreement campaign announcement

policies.title: Six-point immigration plan
policies.summary: ACT proposes tougher deportation rules for serious offending, regular skill checks for work visas, a five-year welfare stand-down for new residents, a temporary-worker infrastructure levy, English requirements and stronger overstayer enforcement.

policies.title: Voting rights for elected council members only
policies.summary: ACT proposes prohibiting unelected members of council committees from having voting or quorum rights.

policies.title: Professional regulator neutrality
policies.summary: ACT proposes stopping professional regulators from disciplining lawful off-duty expression, requiring institutional neutrality, limiting mandatory training and strengthening judicial oversight.

policies.title: 18 ministers and 19 departments
policies.summary: ACT proposes reducing government to 18 ministers and 19 departments, abolishing the Public Service Commission, assigning one minister to each department and allowing ministers to select chief executives.

policies.title: Benefit reassessment and money management
policies.summary: ACT proposes independent medical assessments and reassessments for health and disability benefits, plus mandatory electronic money management for work-ready Jobseeker recipients who remain on the benefit after four months.

policies.title: Dedicated rural crime unit
policies.summary: ACT proposes a dedicated rural crime unit, a target of 100,000 additional rural patrol hours each year and extending the Text 111 service nationwide.

policies.title: Three strikes for burglary
policies.summary: ACT proposes a minimum three-year prison sentence, without parole, home detention or early release, for a third burglary conviction or a conviction containing at least three burglary counts.

policies.title: Limited public-safety powers for licensed security staff
policies.summary: ACT proposes giving appropriately trained and licensed security professionals limited powers to intervene in public-safety incidents.

policies.title: Animal-abuse coercion offence
policies.summary: ACT proposes a specific offence for using or threatening animal abuse to coerce or control another person.

policies.title: Lift medicines funding toward Australian parity
policies.summary: ACT proposes increasing medicines' share of the health budget by one percentage point each year, funded from future health-budget growth, until New Zealand reaches parity with Australia in 2033.

policies.title: Backing Hunters
policies.summary: ACT proposes transferring game-animal management from DOC to the Game Animal Council, recognising game species as valued resources, rewarding verified conservation work and expanding hunter and community roles in access and backcountry maintenance.

policies.title: Remove the charitable-giving tax-credit cap
policies.summary: Opportunity proposes repealing the $100,000 annual cap on donations eligible for the 33% donation tax credit and asking the Law Commission to review charitable regulation.
